text:
Dear Mr Zimmermann,

First the good news: I still have the original purchase receipts for most of what was taken, namely the handbag, the phone and the laptop.

It all happened at home, in my ground-floor flat at Sonnenweg 77 in Kreuzlingen, on the night of 18 to 19 August 2026. It was a very hot night and I'd left the terrace door wide open to get some air while I slept. Someone walked in from the garden and took my handbag from the chair by the door and my laptop from the table next to it. I didn't hear a thing.

I'm enclosing a list of the stolen things with their values, CHF 4,750 altogether.

My keys were in the handbag: flat door, front door of the building and letterbox. Rosenau Cooperative, who own the building, had the cylinders of my flat door and the front door changed the next day and charged me CHF 525. I'd like that included in my claim.

The receipts for the handbag, the phone and the laptop are attached as well.

I should also tell you that I cleaned up the next morning before I'd thought it through. The things the thief didn't want, my diary, make-up and some papers from the handbag, were scattered across the terrace and there were muddy footprints on the floor by the door. I picked everything up and mopped the floor, so none of that can be seen any more. I'm sorry, I just couldn't bear looking at it.

And to be clear about how the thief got in: nothing was forced or broken. No lock, door or window was damaged; the terrace door was simply standing open.

Kind regards,
Eva Ellis
